topics.topic: India’s Rare Earth Strategy: Manufacturing, Corridors, and Global Integration
topics.why_in_news: India accelerated its rare earth strategy focusing on manufacturing ecosystems, strategic corridors and global supply-chain integration to strengthen critical mineral security.
prelims_quick_notes: Rare earth elements (REEs) are critical minerals for advanced technologies.
Used in electronics, EVs, defence systems and renewable energy technologies.
India aims to reduce import dependence for critical minerals.
Rare earth strategy linked with industrial and strategic security.
Supply-chain diversification important amid geopolitical competition.
Critical minerals essential for semiconductor and clean-energy sectors.
India promoting processing and value-addition capabilities.
Global integration important for resilient mineral supply chains.
important_facts: Rare earths include 17 chemically similar elements.
China dominates global rare earth processing capacity.
Critical minerals important for green transition technologies.
India possesses monazite reserves containing rare earth elements.
IREL plays important role in rare earth processing.
Rare earths critical for magnets, batteries and electronics.
key_highlights: Strategic corridors and logistics integration discussed.
Technology partnerships and global cooperation highlighted.
Aim to strengthen domestic industrial ecosystem.
exam_relevance: Important for International Relations, Economy and Strategic Resources.
Useful for supply-chain resilience and critical mineral diplomacy topics.
Can be linked with clean energy transition and industrial policy.
prelims_traps: Rare earth elements are not necessarily geologically rare.
China dominates processing more than raw reserves.
Monazite is important source of rare earth elements in India.
Critical minerals linked with strategic and clean-energy technologies.

topics.topic: India’s Trade Partnerships Powering Global Integration and Growth
topics.why_in_news: India expanded trade partnerships and Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) to strengthen global integration, export competitiveness and resilient supply chains.
prelims_quick_notes: FTAs reduce tariffs and improve market access.
India pursuing strategic trade diversification.
Trade partnerships linked with supply-chain resilience.
FTAs support exports, investments and employment generation.
India expanding trade engagement across Indo-Pacific, Europe and MENA.
Services trade important component of India’s external sector.
Trade diplomacy increasingly linked with geopolitical strategy.
MSMEs expected to benefit from preferential market access.
important_facts: EFTA includes Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.
FTAs aim at tariff liberalisation and regulatory cooperation.
RBI extended export credit tenor to 450 days till March 2026.
key_highlights: India pursuing broader Bilateral Trade Agreement with USA.
Negotiations ongoing with GCC, ASEAN, Mexico and Canada.
Export competitiveness and digital trade facilitation strengthened.
exam_relevance: Important for International Relations, Economy and Trade Policy.
Useful for FTAs, supply chains and economic diplomacy topics.
Can be linked with Make in India and global value chains.
prelims_traps: CEPA and FTA are broader trade partnership mechanisms.
EFTA is not part of European Union.
FTAs include services and investment provisions besides goods trade.
Trade diversification reduces excessive dependence on limited markets.

topics.topic: India and Brazil sign MoU to strengthen and secure steel supply chain
topics.why_in_news: India and Brazil signed MoU to strengthen and secure steel supply chain through cooperation in mining, mineral processing, recycling technologies and AI-driven geoscientific exploration.
prelims_quick_notes: MoU focuses on long-term steel supply-chain cooperation.
India aims to achieve 300 MT steelmaking capacity by 2030.
Steel sector depends heavily on raw materials like coking coal and iron ore.
Brazil important mineral-resource partner for India.
Supply-chain resilience increasingly linked with strategic security.
Cooperation includes mining, recycling and advanced technologies.
Green steel and low-carbon technologies gaining importance.
Steel sector crucial for infrastructure and industrial growth.
important_facts: National Steel Policy, 2017 targets 300 MT capacity by 2030.
India heavily dependent on imported coking coal.
Brazil among major iron ore producers globally.
MoU exchanged in presence of PM Narendra Modi and President Lula da Silva.
Green steel aims to reduce carbon intensity of steel production.
AI-driven geoscientific exploration improves mineral mapping efficiency.
key_highlights: Focus on secure and diversified mineral supply chains.
Cooperation includes technology sharing and automation.
Strategic partnership expanded beyond traditional sectors.
Green and sustainable steel production emphasised.
Supports industrial resilience and manufacturing growth.
exam_relevance: Important for International Relations, Economy and Industrial Policy.
Useful for critical minerals and supply-chain resilience topics.
Can be linked with green manufacturing and strategic partnerships.
prelims_traps: India remains import-dependent for coking coal.
National Steel Policy targets 300 MT capacity by 2030.
Green steel linked with low-carbon industrial processes.
Brazil important partner in mineral-resource cooperation.
